beacons.title: Raymond Zheng
beacons.subtitle: Computer Science · University of Waterloo
beacons.body:
Hi! I'm Raymond, a computer science student at the University of Waterloo. I like figuring out how things work by building them myself.

Each light here covers a bit of what I do. Click one to take a look.

beacons.title: Work
beacons.subtitle: Where I've worked
beacons.body: AI video startup, IT support for the Government of Ontario, event planning for Waterloo's Computer Science Committee, a coding school I founded, a chinese restaurant, and the YMCA.

beacons.title: ViewMax
beacons.subtitle: AI video generation · California · ongoing
beacons.body:
I develop Python tooling and machine learning pipelines to orchestrate AI models for audio and video generation.

I also evaluate the outputs of our tools to improve the consistency and quality of AI-generated media.

beacons.title: Government of Ontario
beacons.subtitle: Systems Support Officer · Toronto · ongoing
beacons.body:
I provide technical support for ministry staff by diagnosing hardware, software, and network issues and getting people back to work quickly.

I also repaired and improved the enterprise LTO tape backup systems, making the backup workflow faster and more reliable.

beacons.title: Waterloo CS Committee
beacons.subtitle: Event Coordinator · Waterloo · 2026
beacons.body:
As event coordinator for the **Waterloo Computer Science Committee**, I ran a recruitment event with an industry partner (ZIP), handling the budget, logistics, and attendee flow on the day.

I also help plan other events and keep membership operations running: registrations, payments, and record tracking.

beacons.title: ByteQuest Academy
beacons.subtitle: Founder · Mississauga · 2024
beacons.body:
I founded a ten-week coding program for twenty students and volunteers, handling everything from curriculum design to teaching.

The course covered Scratch and Python, built around projects the students picked themselves. The goal was to make programming feel approachable; most of them kept going after the program ended.

beacons.title: China China Palace
beacons.subtitle: Storefront Manager · Mississauga · 2024
beacons.body:
I managed the storefront of a busy restaurant: coordinating the team through peak hours, running daily closing procedures, and handling customer issues on the spot.

Good practice for staying organized when six things need attention at once.

beacons.title: YMCA of Greater Toronto
beacons.subtitle: Swim Instructor / Lifeguard · Mississauga · 2023
beacons.body:
I taught swim lessons and lifeguarded at the YMCA of Greater Toronto Area. Teaching means breaking a skill down until a 5 year old can do it; guarding means staying alert for hours at a stretch.

Both have made me more patient and a clearer communicator.

beacons.title: Projects
beacons.subtitle: Things I've built
beacons.body: Most of these started with the same question: how does this actually work? So I built my own. A deep learning framework, a physics engine, a voice-controlled drone, and a Minecraft server that grew to thirty thousand players.

beacons.title: Nimbus
beacons.subtitle: A multimodal AI drone system · 2026
beacons.body:
A drone you can fly by talking to it. Speech recognition and intent extraction turn natural language into flight commands, while computer vision gives the drone spatial awareness; all in real time.

A FastAPI backend connects **Gemini** for language understanding, **YOLOv8** for vision, and **ElevenLabs** for voice to a Swift app driving the DJI SDK.

beacons.title: NimbleML
beacons.subtitle: A deep learning framework · ongoing
beacons.body:
A deep learning framework I wrote from scratch to understand what PyTorch actually does; over forty neural network modules, automatic differentiation, GPU acceleration, and transformer architectures.

To prove it works, I built a GPT on top of it: BPE tokenization, fused kernels, flash attention, and mixed CPU/GPU execution.

beacons.title: Kinematica
beacons.subtitle: Real-time 3D physics engine · 2025
beacons.body:
A real-time 3D physics engine with soft-body and rigid-body dynamics, GJK collision detection for arbitrary meshes, and custom solvers.

It includes a material loading system for creating and configuring physics bodies, so you can prototype complex mechanics without touching solver code.

beacons.title: Post-It
beacons.subtitle: AR lens for Snapchat Spectacles · 2025
beacons.body:
An augmented reality lens for Snapchat Spectacles, built with Snap3D and controlled entirely by hand gestures.

Built at **Hack the North 2025**, where it placed in the top 32 out of more than a thousand participants.

beacons.title: MHDungeon
beacons.subtitle: A Minecraft world, 30,000 players · 2025
beacons.body:
A large-scale Minecraft server with custom gameplay written in Skript against the Bukkit API; dungeon generation, enemy scaling, parties, pathfinding, bosses, and reward systems.

It grew past **30,000 unique players**. I scaled the infrastructure, fixed production issues live, and shipped new content on a running server. I also handled the marketing and community side, which cleared **$8,000** in profit.

beacons.title: Link
beacons.subtitle: Matching students to extracurriculars · 2024
beacons.body:
A platform that helps students find extracurriculars in their community. Members create and join communities, post upcoming activities, and the matchmaking system pairs each post with the students most likely to care about it.

Built at **EducateHacks 2024**: a Python **websockets** backend with **MongoDB** for storage, and a hand-rolled HTML/CSS/JavaScript front end.

beacons.title: Armada Foundry
beacons.subtitle: A progressive tank-building game
beacons.body: A progressive tank-building game made in **Unity**. You design your own tank and keep upgrading it as you play.

beacons.title: About
beacons.subtitle: The short version
beacons.body:
I'm a computer science student at the University of Waterloo, in the co-op program. Right now I'm most interested in machine learning systems: kernels, autograd, attention, the machinery underneath the frameworks.

Outside of code, I swimm, and I've run everything from coding classes to campus events.

beacons.title: Education
beacons.body:
**University of Waterloo** — Bachelor of Computer Science (BCS), Co-operative Program. Sep 2025 – Jun 2030, Waterloo, ON.

**Google** — Data Analytics Professional Certificate. Jan 2024 – Jun 2024.

beacons.title: Skills
beacons.subtitle: What I reach for
beacons.body:
**Languages** — Python, C++, C#, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Racket, Skript.

**Machine learning** — PyTorch, TensorFlow, Scikit-learn, NumPy, CuPy, OpenCV, autograd, transformer architectures.

**Data** — Pandas, Matplotlib, SQL, MongoDB, data processing, augmentation, dataset analysis.

**Also** — React Native, Flask, Expo, .NET, raylib, OpenMP, GPU programming, computational geometry, real-time systems.

beacons.title: Contact
beacons.subtitle: Say hello
beacons.body: I'm looking for co-op roles in machine learning. Email is the fastest way to reach me; I read everything.
